QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_122

question.text: Following the SEBI October 2024 revision of index derivatives contract sizes, which of the following would be a COMPLIANT lot size for an index futures contract at an index level of 3,000?

answer.text: Lot size of 500 (contract value = 3,000 x 500 = Rs. 15,00,000 = Rs. 15 lakhs, within the Rs. 15-20 lakh range)
Lot size of 100 (contract value = Rs. 3,00,000 = Rs. 3 lakhs, below the range)
Lot size of 1,000 (contract value = Rs. 30,00,000 = Rs. 30 lakhs, above the range)
Lot size of 50 (contract value = Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 1.5 lakhs, well below the range)

explanation.text: The Logic: The source frames the October 2024 change as a revision of index derivatives contract sizes. For an index level of 3,000, contract value = index x lot size. A lot size of 500 gives 3,000 x 500 = Rs. 15,00,000 = Rs. 15 lakhs, which is the lower bound of the prescribed Rs. 15-20 lakh range; the other options fall well outside it. The Trap: The Rs. 15-20 lakh contract-value range, as cited in the source, is presented as an index derivatives measure - applying it to a single stock price would be a different regulatory question. Note: Source: NISM-Series-VIII workbook (Dec 2025), pages 32 and 172.
